answer: Job 01a15f9f-2d47-72de-9aaf-a27c336423fa on garnet:mock, 100 shots, completed. Counts: 00 = 56, 11 = 44. That is a clean Bell pair between QB1 and QB2, with both measured under key m. I made two fixes. First, QB25 does not exist on garnet, which has QB1 to QB20 only, so I used QB2, which is coupled to QB1. Second, cx is not a native IQM gate. The native two-qubit gate is cz, and the allowed pair is listed as [QB2, QB1], so I used that order. To rebuild the CNOT, I put a prx(pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB1 to make the superposition. On QB2 I put a prx(pi/2, pi/2) before the cz and a prx(-pi/2, pi/2) after it, which together act like a Hadamard on each side of the cz. I submitted the fixed circuit once. The mock is noise-free, so the counts are not a test of hardware quality. The fixed circuit is saved at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_3612af23-e49-17/bell_fixed.json.
